title: Torus Berry Data Determine All-Genus Abelian Topological Orders
abstract: We show that for Abelian Chern-Simons topological orders, torus Berry matrices determine the all-genus extended TQFT. We identify the topological part of the projective Berry holonomy under metric deformations with the mapping-class-group representation of the Abelian Chern-Simons TQFT and prove that the normalized torus data reconstruct its finite quadratic module $(G,q)$. Recent work showed that $(G,q)$ classifies the extended theory up to symmetric monoidal natural isomorphism, then genus-one data determine the all-genus theory without choosing a $K$-matrix presentation. We also prove that, for normalized character row errors $δ<21.96$%, nearest-row decoding recovers the Abelian fusion algebra independently of the number of anyons. The result applies to Abelian fractional quantum Hall and spin-liquid phases described by even-lattice Chern-Simons theories.
summary: This paper establishes that for Abelian topological orders, the information encoded in torus Berry matrices is sufficient to uniquely determine the entire topological quantum field theory across all genera. By linking the Berry holonomy to the mapping-class group representation, the authors provide a robust, numerically verifiable method to characterize exotic quantum phases like fractional quantum Hall states.
main_problem: The core problem is determining if the topological order of an Abelian Chern-Simons theory can be fully reconstructed from measurements of torus Berry matrices, even when those measurements are subject to finite errors.
main_result: The authors prove that for Abelian Chern-Simons topological orders, the torus Berry matrices are sufficient to determine the entire all-genus extended TQFT, and this reconstruction is stable against small measurement errors.
method: The work combines geometric quantization techniques (involving half-forms and BKS maps) with algebraic reconstruction methods, specifically using nearest-row decoding on measured Berry data to recover the underlying finite quadratic module (G, q).
model_or_system: The study focuses on Abelian Chern-Simons topological orders, which are relevant to physical systems like Abelian fractional quantum Hall states and spin-liquid phases described by even-lattice Chern-Simons theories.
key_observables: Torus Berry matrices (S, T), the finite quadratic module (G, q), and the projective Berry holonomy.
important_parameters: The error bound $\delta < 21.96\%$ is critical for the successful reconstruction of the fusion algebra.
main_assumptions: The reconstruction is strictly proven for Abelian theories; the analysis also relies on fixing a topological basis and assuming the theory is Abelian.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the 'Berry tomography map,' demonstrating how torus Berry transport reconstructs the quadratic module (G, q), which in turn fixes the all-genus extended theory.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by first establishing the mathematical link between the projective Berry holonomy and the mapping-class-group representation of the TQFT. It then tackles the reconstruction problem by showing that the measured torus data uniquely determines the algebraic structure (G, q), culminating in the proof that this structure fixes the entire TQFT.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, experimentally verifiable diagnostic tool for characterizing exotic topological phases of matter, linking abstract mathematical structures (TQFTs) directly to measurable quantities (Berry phases) in condensed matter systems.
